name: Paramount+ Design System
summary: Broadcast-bold iOS design tokens and component specs distilled from Paramount+'s navy-and-blue network-bundle streaming app.
description: A reference kit pulling the hex palette, Inter type ramp, and signature component measurements out of Paramount+'s iOS app so you can restyle a streaming or hybrid-content app in the same broadcast-network idiom.

whatYouGet: The full midnight-navy palette (canvas #0A0E2D, hero-lift #0E1438, three surface steps, divider, three text tiers) plus the single Paramount+ Blue #0064FF accent and its #0052CC pressed state
A 13-row Inter type ramp (Paramount Sans's free stand-in) running from a 32pt/900 screen title down to an 8pt/800 uppercase badge, each with exact line-height and tracking
Measurements for the brand-hubs chip row, hero billboard, poster card, live badge, keep-watching progress bar, and bottom tab bar, including corner radii and padding
The 4pt spacing scale and an eight-step border-radius scale running from square hero art to a 500pt pill
A motion table covering the hub re-skin cross-fade, hero auto-rotate, poster press, and live-dot pulse with exact durations and easing curves
A six-breakpoint responsive table (iPhone SE through iPad landscape) plus Dynamic Type and safe-area handling notes
content.promptText:
<role>You are a senior iOS design engineer who has spent years shipping production SwiftUI apps for ad-and-subscription hybrid streaming platforms. You know how to translate a broadcast network's on-air branding into a coherent mobile design system, and you default to giving exact, implementable values rather than vague direction.</role>

<reference_data>
Source inspiration: a network-bundle streaming app built around a deep navy canvas rather than pure black, with one disciplined accent color carrying every interactive moment.

COLOR (dark-only product):
- Canvas #0A0E2D, Canvas-under-hero #0E1438, Surface 1 #161C44, Surface 2 #1F2655, Divider #2A3266
- Text: Primary #FFFFFF, Secondary #AEB4D6, Tertiary #6F77A6
- Single accent: Primary Blue #0064FF (pressed #0052CC), Sky/active-tab tint #4D9DFF, Glass fill rgba(255,255,255,0.14)
- Semantic: Live/sports red #FF2D46, Success #1ED760, Error #FF453A, Rating gold #F5C518

TYPOGRAPHY (Inter as the free substitute for a proprietary grotesque):
- Screen title 32pt/900, line-height 1.05, tracking -0.6pt
- Hero title 26pt/800, 1.02, -0.5pt
- Row header 22pt/700, 1.15, -0.2pt
- Card title 18pt/700
- Body 16pt/600 (and a 16pt/400 regular variant for long-form copy)
- Caption 15pt/500, Meta 13pt/400, Poster caption 11pt/500
- Tab label 12pt/600, Eyebrow 11pt/800 uppercase with +1.6pt tracking, Button 15pt/700, Badge 8pt/800 uppercase

COMPONENTS:
- Primary button: 6pt radius, fill #0064FF, white Inter 15pt/700 label, 13pt/28pt padding, pressed → #0052CC + scale 0.98
- Glass secondary button: rgba(255,255,255,0.14) with 6px blur, 6pt radius
- Poster card: 2:3 ratio, ~116pt wide, 8pt radius, optional red LIVE flag (4pt radius, 5pt pulsing dot) or blue NEW badge
- Brand-hub chip: ~70pt min-width x 40pt, 8pt radius, filled with a per-network brand gradient, tapping re-skins the whole browse surface into that network's color
- Hero billboard: ~46% of screen height, bottom scrim linear-gradient(180deg, transparent 36%, rgba(10,14,45,0.72) 70%, canvas 100%)
- Live badge: #FF2D46 fill, 4pt radius, 11pt/800 uppercase, 5pt/10pt padding, leading pulsing white dot
- Progress bar: 4pt track height, 2pt radius, track #1F2655, fill #0064FF solid
- Bottom tab bar: 64pt + safe area, rgba(10,14,45,0.96) with 18px blur + 160% saturation, active tab = filled #4D9DFF glyph, inactive = stroked #6F77A6

LAYOUT:
- Base spacing unit 4pt; scale 4/8/12/16/18/24/32/40/48/64
- Content inset 18pt; poster gap 10pt; hub chip gap 8pt
- Radius scale: 0 (full-bleed art), 4pt (badges), 6pt (buttons), 8pt (cards/chips), 12pt (tooltips), 20pt (sheets), 500pt (pills), 50% (circles)

MOTION:
- Hub re-skin cross-fade 300ms ease-in-out; hero auto-rotate cross-fade 400ms every ~8s; poster press scale 1.0→0.97 over 120ms ease-out; live-dot pulse opacity 1→0.4→1 over 1.2s infinite; sheet present 300ms ease-out
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never let the single accent color sit behind a body-text block — reserve it for fills on CTAs, progress, and selection rings only, because the source system's entire identity rests on that restraint reading as deliberate rather than accidental.
2. Keep the canvas a tinted dark (not pure black) — a slight hue lift under hero art is what makes full-color key art look lit rather than sitting on a hole in the screen.
3. Give live/breaking content its own reserved color, never the primary accent — a viewer should be able to tell this is happening now from color alone before reading any text.
4. Treat any category-chip row as a structural anchor, not a decoration — if a brand or bundle identity depends on it, it goes above the hero, not below, or the hierarchy reads backwards.
5. Cap corner radius on content art (posters, thumbnails) at 6–8pt — heavier rounding starts to look like a card game, not a media catalog.
6. Use scale-based press feedback (0.96–0.98) instead of color-flash feedback on dark surfaces — color flashes are hard to time consistently across mixed-brightness art, scale reads reliably every time.
7. Fix the type size of anything composited directly over image content (badges, eyebrows, tab labels) — Dynamic Type scaling on those breaks the layout math against art that isn't scaling with it.
8. Keep motion under ~400ms for anything that isn't a continuous status indicator (like a live pulse) — a broadcast-adjacent app needs to feel quick and current, not deliberate and cinematic.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / working title: ___
- Content vertical (e.g. sports, kids, prestige drama, live news): ___
- Is this a single-brand app or a bundle of multiple sub-brands/channels?: ___
- Primary accent color (hex, or pick one for me): ___
- Verb on the primary CTA (Play / Watch / Listen / Read): ___
- Does the app carry a live component that needs its own visual treatment?: ___
- Existing design tokens or brand guidelines to reconcile with (paste or describe): ___
- Target iOS minimum version and any Android/tvOS parity requirement: ___
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete SwiftUI Color and Font token file for the project, mapped from the reference palette/type ramp onto the user's own brand color and font choice, preserving the same structural roles (canvas, canvas-under-hero, three surfaces, three text tiers, one accent, one live/status color).
2. Adapted specs for the four signature components (bundle/category row if applicable, hero billboard, content card, progress/status indicator), each with exact radius, padding, and state changes translated to the new brand.
3. A bottom tab bar spec (height, blur, active/inactive treatment) matching the reference's material and state-change pattern.
4. A motion and haptics table listing every animated state (press, live pulse, hero rotation, re-skin/transition if relevant) with duration and easing, calibrated to the reference's pacing.
5. A responsive table across at least four breakpoints (small phone, standard phone, large phone, tablet) describing what changes at each.
6. A short do's-and-don'ts list (6–10 items) specific to this project, written in the same disciplined-restraint spirit as the house rules above.
7. An accessibility pass: which text scales with Dynamic Type vs. stays fixed, contrast notes for text-on-accent-fill pairings, and how any color-only status signal (like live) gets a redundant non-color cue.
</what_to_give_me>
install: Open this Starter and copy the full prompt text into Claude, ChatGPT, or your in-editor AI assistant.
Fill in the <the_project> fields with your app's name, content vertical, brand color, and platform target.
Ask for the token file first (colors + fonts), review it against your actual brand guidelines, then request the component specs one at a time.
Paste the resulting SwiftUI Color/Font extensions straight into your project and wire the component specs into your existing views.

description: A reference kit that extracts Peacock's indigo-black palette, Poppins type ramp, and signature feather-gradient rules so you can apply the same glow-in-the-dark, single-gradient-accent approach to another streaming or media app.

whatYouGet: The indigo-black palette (canvas #0A0A14, warm hero canvas #140E26, three surface steps, divider, three text tiers) plus the five-stop feather gradient (#FACC15 → #F97316 → #EC4899 → #8B5CF6 → #2563EB)
The full Poppins-based type ramp, weights 400 through 800, from an 11pt/700 uppercase eyebrow to a 32pt/800 screen title
Exact specs for the hero billboard with centered logo lockup, the channel tile rail, Top-10 rank-numeral treatment, and the always-white primary CTA
The rule set for where the gradient is and isn't allowed to appear (logomark, upsell, selection — never behind text, never over art)
A motion table covering hero cross-fade, poster press, live-dot pulse, and progress-fill animation with exact durations
A responsive breakpoint table plus Dynamic Type, orientation, and touch-target rules
content.promptText:
<role>You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in premium video-streaming apps, with deep experience translating a multi-color brand mark into a disciplined mobile UI system without letting the gradient take over the whole screen.</role>

<reference_data>
Source inspiration: a permanently-dark streaming app where a five-color gradient is the entire chromatic identity, kept out of body copy and reserved for a short list of brand moments, while the primary action button is stark white for maximum contrast.

COLOR (dark-only):
- Canvas #0A0A14, Canvas-warm-under-hero #140E26, Surface 1 #1A1530, Surface 2 #241C3D, Divider #2C2545
- Text: Primary #FFFFFF, Secondary #B5B2C2, Tertiary #7A7689
- CTA: white #FFFFFF fill with near-black #0A0A14 label (never brand-tinted), pressed #E6E6EA
- Five-stop gradient: Yellow #FACC15, Orange #F97316, Pink #EC4899, Purple #8B5CF6, Blue #2563EB — used only for logomark, premium-upsell buttons, and selection/progress accents
- Semantic: Live red #E5142B, Success #1DB954, Error #FF453A

TYPOGRAPHY (Poppins as the free substitute for a proprietary geometric grotesque):
- Screen title 32pt/800, Hero title 28pt/800, Row header 22pt/700, Card title 18pt/700
- Body 16pt/600 (plus 16pt/400 regular for long copy)
- Caption 15pt/500, Meta 13pt/400, Poster caption 11pt/500
- Tab label 12pt/600, Eyebrow 11pt/700 uppercase +1.4pt tracking, Button 15pt/700
- Rank numeral 13pt/800 tabular, Badge 10pt/800 uppercase +0.4pt tracking

COMPONENTS:
- Primary button: always white fill #FFFFFF, near-black #0A0A14 label, 6pt radius, 13pt/26pt padding, pressed → #E6E6EA + scale 0.98
- Premium-upsell button: gradient fill (orange→pink subset or full 5-stop on large CTAs), 6pt radius — the only place the gradient is a button fill
- Poster card: 2:3 ratio, ~112pt wide, 8pt radius, optional rank numeral in a 45%-black pill or gradient TOP-10/NEW badge
- Channel tile: 60x60pt, 14pt radius, network-brand gradient fill, live tiles get a red LIVE pill
- Hero billboard: ~50% of screen height, centered composition, logo lockup replaces text title for Originals
- Progress bar (Continue Watching): 4pt track, 2pt radius, gradient fill (orange→pink)
- Bottom tab bar: 64pt + safe area, white filled active icon (not colored), no tint pill

LAYOUT:
- 4pt base spacing unit, scale 4/8/12/16/18/24/32/40/48/64
- Radius scale: 0 (hero/scrims), 4pt (badges/pills), 6pt (buttons/cards/search), 14pt (channel tiles), 20pt (sheets), 500pt (pills), 50% (circles)

MOTION:
- Hero cross-fade 400ms ease-in-out every ~8s; poster press 1.0→0.97 over 120ms ease-out; live-dot pulse 1→0.4→1 over 1.2s infinite; progress fill 0→value over 400ms on appear
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never tint the single most-used CTA with the brand gradient or brand color if maximum contrast against varied artwork is the goal — a neutral (white or near-black) button reads instantly on any background, a tinted one can wash out on similarly-hued art.
2. Restrict a multi-stop gradient to identity and monetization moments (logo, upsell, selection) — using it as a large background fill or body-text color turns a signature mark into visual noise.
3. If Top-N or ranked-content rows exist, give the rank number its own high-weight numeral style distinct from the title type — a rank needs to be scannable in under a second from a couch's distance.
4. Keep a live/status accent completely separate from the brand gradient/color — status colors need to be readable as different from everything else, which fails if they share hue family with the brand.
5. Center-align only the hero composition; keep list/row content left-aligned — mixing alignment models inside one screen reads as inconsistent rather than intentional.
6. Fix gradient direction and stop order as a reusable asset, don't let each screen invent its own gradient angle — consistency in the gradient's direction is what makes it recognizable as a mark rather than a random decorative color.
7. Use scale + shadow together for pressed states on dark surfaces, not opacity alone — opacity changes are hard to perceive against near-black canvases.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / working title: ___
- Content vertical (drama, sports, kids, live TV, etc.): ___
- Brand's primary mark: single color or a multi-stop gradient? (describe or paste swatches): ___
- Does the primary CTA need to be neutral/white, or brand-tinted?: ___
- Does the catalog have a live TV / channels component, ranked lists, or both?: ___
- Existing typography (brand font + any open-source fallback already chosen): ___
- Target iOS minimum version and any tvOS/web parity need: ___
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI Color + LinearGradient + Font token file mapped from the reference onto the user's own brand palette, preserving the same structural split between neutral CTA, brand gradient/color for identity only, and reserved status color.
2. Adapted specs for the hero billboard (with or without a logo-lockup variant), the primary content card, and any channel-tile or ranked-list component the project needs.
3. Explicit written rules for exactly where the brand gradient/color is and is not allowed to appear, in the same restraint-first spirit as the reference.
4. A motion table (hero rotation, card press, status pulse, progress fill) with concrete durations and easing.
5. A bottom tab bar spec matching the reference's active/inactive treatment pattern.
6. A responsive table across at least 4 breakpoints plus Dynamic Type guidance (what scales, what stays fixed and why).
7. A short accessibility note on contrast for the CTA and any color-only status signal, with a non-color redundant cue proposed for each.
</what_to_give_me>
install: Copy this prompt into Claude, ChatGPT, or your assistant of choice.
Fill in <the_project> with your app's brand color/gradient, content type, and platform target.
Request the token file and gradient-usage rules first, confirm they match your brand guidelines, then ask for each component spec in turn.
Drop the generated SwiftUI tokens into your Xcode project and apply the component specs to your existing screens.

name: Plex Design System
summary: Calm-utility iOS design tokens from Plex, centered on a cool-charcoal canvas, one disciplined yellow accent, and a signature multi-server picker.
description: A reference kit distilling Plex's charcoal palette, Inter type ramp, and server-picker/On-Deck component specs for anyone building a personal-media, self-hosted, or multi-source app that needs a calm rather than commercial tone.

whatYouGet: The cool-charcoal palette (canvas #1F2326, three surface steps, divider) plus the single Plex Yellow #E5A00D accent and its mandatory dark-ink (#1A1304) text pairing rule
A full Inter type ramp from a 32pt/800 screen title down to a 10pt/600 tab label, tuned for a functional, not expressive tone
Exact specs for the server-picker pill and sheet, the On Deck resume tile with centered play overlay, and the unwatched-item corner dot
Server status color coding (#4CAF50 online / #6B7075 offline) and where the yellow accent is and isn't allowed to appear (max ~5 roles per screen)
A calm motion table (150–280ms, no bounce) covering server switch, resume, and status-dot transitions
A responsive breakpoint table plus touch-target and safe-area rules
content.promptText:
<role>You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in personal-media and self-hosted software — apps where the product is presenting the user's own content rather than selling a catalog, and where the UI needs to read as calm utility rather than commercial spectacle.</role>

<reference_data>
Source inspiration: a personal media-server client that deliberately avoids true black in favor of a cool charcoal canvas, uses exactly one accent color across roughly five defined roles, and is one of the few streaming-style apps with a first-class multi-server picker.

COLOR (dark-first, not true black):
- Canvas #1F2326 (deliberately not #000000), Surface 1 #282C30, Surface 2 #32373B, Surface 3 #3C4146, Divider #34393D
- Text: Primary #F2F3F4, Secondary #9BA0A4, Tertiary #6B7075
- Single accent: Plex Yellow #E5A00D, pressed #C98A09, mandatory dark ink on any yellow fill #1A1304 (never white-on-yellow)
- Status: Online green #4CAF50, Offline gray #6B7075, Error #E5484D

TYPOGRAPHY (Inter, matching the app's neutral, legible tone):
- Screen title 32pt/800, Hero title 26pt/800, Section header 22pt/700, Subsection 18pt/700
- Body 16pt/400, Card title 15pt/600, Meta line 14pt/400, Button label 16pt/700
- Server name 14pt/600, Server meta 12pt/400, Tab label 10pt/600, Tech/caption chip 12pt/600 with +0.2pt tracking

COMPONENTS:
- Primary button (Play): 8pt radius, yellow #E5A00D fill, dark-ink #1A1304 label — never white, 14pt/28pt padding, pressed → #C98A09 + scale 0.98
- Server picker pill: fully rounded (999pt), #282C30 fill, 1pt #34393D border, status dot + name + chevron, 7pt/14pt padding
- Server sheet row: 8pt radius, #32373B (unselected) or #3C4146 (selected), status dot + name + meta, yellow checkmark on the selected row
- On Deck tile: 16:9, 6pt radius, centered 42pt play-overlay circle on rgba(0,0,0,0.55), yellow progress bar pinned to the bottom edge
- Poster card: 2:3, 6pt radius, single 9pt yellow unwatched dot top-right with a small shadow for legibility
- Bottom tab bar: 50pt + safe area, yellow active icon+label, gray inactive, no tint pill

LAYOUT:
- 4pt base spacing unit, scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/28/32/40/48/64
- Screen inset 20pt, poster grid gutter 12pt
- Radius scale: 0 (dividers/art edges), 4pt (chips/badges), 6pt (posters/On Deck), 8pt (buttons/rows/sheets-content), 12pt (bottom sheets), 500pt (pills), 50% (status dots/avatars)

MOTION:
- Server switch: check fades in 150ms, sheet dismisses 250ms, content cross-fades 250ms; On Deck resume: press scale 150ms then progress bar animates 0→watched over 350ms ease-out; status dot transitions cross-fade 200ms with no bounce
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Use a tinted dark neutral instead of true black for any app whose product is personal or user-owned content — pure black reads as void, a slightly warm or cool charcoal reads as calm room, which matters when someone browses for long stretches.
2. Cap a single accent color to a hard, named list of roles (5 or fewer) and write that list down — an accent that creeps into every button and label stops signaling anything special.
3. Any fill using the single accent color must pair with a dedicated dark or light ink token chosen for contrast, decided once and applied everywhere — inconsistent text-on-accent choices are one of the fastest ways a UI looks unpolished.
4. If the product can connect to more than one backend/source/account, surface which one is active persistently, not buried in settings — this is core orientation information, not administrative chrome.
5. Model status (online/offline, connected/disconnected) with a small, consistently-placed colored dot plus a text label — never color alone, and never a differently-shaped indicator in different places.
6. Prefer surface-color steps over drop shadows for elevation on a flat, calm-toned canvas — heavy shadows read as trying too hard against a deliberately quiet palette.
7. Keep motion timing in the 150–280ms range with ease-out and no spring/bounce for a calm-utility product — bounce reads as playful, which fights a trustworthy home appliance tone.
8. Give an in-progress or resume item a persistent progress indicator rather than a badge or label alone — a progress bar communicates exactly how much is left at a glance, a label requires reading.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / working title: ___
- What kind of content/source does this app present (personal library, multi-account aggregator, single-source catalog)?: ___
- Does it need to support switching between multiple backends/servers/accounts?: ___
- Preferred single accent color (hex, or pick something warm/cool for me): ___
- Tone target: calm utility, energetic marketplace, or something else — describe in a phrase: ___
- Existing typography choice, if any: ___
- Target iOS minimum version: ___
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI Color + Font token file mapped from the reference onto the user's brand accent and tone, preserving the charcoal-not-black canvas philosophy and the accent-role discipline.
2. If applicable, a source/account picker component spec (pill + sheet) modeled on the reference's server picker, including status-dot color coding.
3. A resume/in-progress content tile spec with a progress indicator, plus a standard content-grid card spec with an unobtrusive status dot.
4. A calm motion table (source switch, card press, status change) with durations and easing matched to the reference's restrained pacing.
5. A bottom tab bar spec.
6. A short list of accent-usage rules specific to this project (which roles get the accent, which don't) written in the same disciplined tone as the house rules above.
7. Accessibility notes: the mandatory contrast pairing for any accent-color fill, and how status is conveyed without relying on color alone.
</what_to_give_me>
install: Copy the prompt into your AI assistant of choice.
Fill in <the_project> — especially whether your app needs a multi-source/server picker.
Ask for the token file and accent-usage rules first, then request each component spec.
Apply the generated SwiftUI tokens and component measurements to your existing views.

name: Pluto TV Design System
summary: iOS design tokens for a live-TV channel-guide app, extracted from Pluto TV's frozen-frame EPG grid, on-now yellow signature, and cobalt-blue brand system.
description: A reference kit pulling the exact colors, type, and grid mechanics out of Pluto TV's iOS app for anyone building a linear/EPG-style live-TV guide rather than a poster-wall streaming app.

whatYouGet: The deep cool-navy palette (canvas #0B0F1F, three surface steps, divider) plus Pluto Blue #0048FF, signature on-now yellow #FFE100, and link cyan #00C2FF
A tabular-numeral Manrope type ramp built specifically for grid alignment, from a 32pt/800 display size down to a 10pt/700 sticky time-bar label
Full mechanics for the EPG (electronic program guide) grid: frozen channel column, sticky 30-minute time-bar, and the signature On Now cell treatment (brighter surface + 3pt yellow left border)
The pinned mini-player spec (LIVE chip, channel line, program title, elapsed-progress bar) and the now-playing compact bar variant
A motion table for channel-surfing cross-fades, timeline/time-bar scroll sync, and category-pill filtering
A responsive breakpoint table showing how channel-column width and visible time-slots change across devices
content.promptText:
<role>You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in live-TV and EPG (electronic program guide) interfaces — the kind of grid-based, frozen-frame layout that behaves differently from a typical poster-wall streaming app and has its own alignment and scroll-sync requirements.</role>

<reference_data>
Source inspiration: a free ad-supported live-TV app whose entire identity is a channel guide grid rather than a content catalog, built on a navy canvas with a strict two-color system — blue for brand/action, yellow reserved exclusively for this is airing right now.

COLOR (dark-only):
- Canvas #0B0F1F, Surface 1 #141A2E, Surface 2 #1C2440 (the on now surface), Surface 3 #25304F, Divider #2A3556
- Brand: Pluto Blue #0048FF (pressed #0039CC, bright #2C6BFF), Pluto Yellow #FFE100 (text on it #0B0F1F), Pluto Cyan #00C2FF (links)
- Text: Primary #FFFFFF, Secondary #9DA8C7 (cool slate, never warm gray), Tertiary #6B7595
- Live Red #FF3B5C for the universal LIVE dot/label; Success #21D07A; Error #FF4A6E

TYPOGRAPHY (Manrope, tabular figures mandatory for grid alignment):
- Display 32pt/800, Screen title 24pt/800, Section 20pt/700, Now Playing 17pt/700
- Body 15pt/400, Channel name 13pt/700, Program title 13pt/600, Meta/schedule 12pt/500
- Channel number 10pt/800 tabular, Time-bar label 10pt/700 tabular, Live/On-Now badge 10pt/800 uppercase, Tab label 10pt/600

COMPONENTS (the EPG grid is the core structural idea):
- Fixed channel column: 86pt wide, 64pt row height, channel number (tabular) stacked over a ~40x28pt logo tile (5pt radius, per-channel gradient)
- Sticky time-bar: 30-minute increments, offset by the channel-column width, scrolls horizontally in lockstep with the program timeline, stays pinned while rows scroll vertically
- EPG program cell: idle #141A2E fill with a 1pt gap-line; the On Now cell gets #1C2440 fill PLUS a 3pt #FFE100 left border — this is the single most recognizable signature in the whole app
- Mini-player (pinned top, ~150pt tall): LIVE chip (red dot + white label on rgba(0,0,0,0.4)), channel line in cyan, program title 18pt/800, thin yellow elapsed-progress bar
- Category-tier pills: cable-box-style genre filters, idle #1C2440/active #0048FF, fully rounded
- Bottom tab bar: 54pt + safe area, yellow active icon/label, no pill indicator

LAYOUT:
- 4pt base spacing unit, scale 4/6/8/10/12/16/20/24/32/40/48
- EPG row height fixed at 64pt; channel column fixed at 86pt; program-cell padding 8pt vertical / 10pt horizontal
- Radius scale: 0 (EPG cells/channel tiles/time-bar — deliberately rectilinear, not card-like), 4pt (progress/ad ticks), 5-6pt (logo tiles), 8pt (buttons/search/cards), 10-12pt (posters/sheets), 999pt (category pills)

MOTION:
- Channel-surf tune-in cross-fades the mini-player video ~300ms; time-bar and program timeline scroll bound to the same offset so they move together instantly; category filter swap cross-fades rows 200ms; optional on-now border can breathe 0.85↔1.0 opacity over 2s (kept minimal)
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Keep the channel-identifier column and any time-axis header frozen while only the content grid scrolls — a real TV guide never lets you lose track of which channel or time slot you're looking at, and neither should this.
2. Use tabular (monospaced) figures for every number that appears in a fixed-width column — channel numbers and times must not cause column drift as digits change.
3. Give a live/current-airing item exactly one unmistakable visual signature (a colored border, a badge, a background shift — pick one primary cue) and use it nowhere else in the product, so on now is instantly recognizable without reading text.
4. Keep grid cells rectilinear (square or near-square corners) rather than card-rounded — a broadcast grid reads as organized information, not a stack of app cards, and rounding it undercuts that.
5. Never use drop shadows inside the grid itself — use surface brightness steps for hierarchy; shadows on a dense, flat grid create visual noise at grid density.
6. Reserve a signature accent color for exactly one meaning (e.g. airing now) and use a separate brand color for everything else interactive — blending the two into one all-purpose accent erases the very signal the guide depends on.
7. Use cool-toned secondary/tertiary text (slate/blue-gray) on a navy canvas rather than neutral warm gray — warm gray visibly clashes with a blue-based dark palette.
8. Keep channel-surfing and filter transitions fast (150–300ms) — a live-TV guide is meant to feel like flipping channels, not like navigating a deliberate cinematic app.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / working title: ___
- Is this primarily a live/linear channel guide, a hybrid live+on-demand app, or something else?: ___
- Approximate number of channels/rows the guide needs to display at once: ___
- Brand color(s) for action/CTA vs. the reserved on now signal color: ___
- Does the app need a pinned mini-player while browsing the guide?: ___
- Existing typography choice, if any (must support tabular figures well): ___
- Target iOS minimum version and device targets (phone only / phone+tablet): ___
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI Color + Font token file mapped onto the user's brand, preserving the strict two-role color split (brand/action vs. reserved on now/live signal).
2. A full EPG grid component spec: frozen channel column, sticky time-bar, idle vs. on-now program cell states, with exact dimensions and the sync behavior between the time-bar and the scrolling timeline.

content.promptText:
<role>You are a senior iOS design engineer experienced in building hybrid subscription-plus-storefront video apps — ones that mix included content with paid add-on channels in the same feed — and in designing contextual overlays that layer information onto a playing video without interrupting it.</role>

<reference_data>
Source inspiration: a cinema-and-storefront hybrid streaming app on a dark blue-slate canvas (not neutral black), with a single bright accent reserved for the primary action verb, and a signature contextual overlay that surfaces cast/scene info without pausing playback.

COLOR:
- Canvas #0F171E (blue-slate, not neutral black — pure #000000 is reserved for the video player only), Surface 1 #1A242F, Surface 2 #232F3E, Surface 3/Divider #2E3B47
- Text: Primary #FFFFFF, Secondary #AAB7C4, Tertiary #6E7B89
- Accent: Prime Blue #00A8E1 (pressed #008CBD), with a deliberate rule that text ON the blue CTA is dark-navy #0F171E, not white — this is intentional for contrast on a bright cyan-blue
- Semantic: IMDb-family yellow #F5C518 (a badge, not an accent), Live/Error red #E50914

TYPOGRAPHY (Amazon Ember, Inter as free fallback — weights limited to 400/600/700 only):
- Details title 30pt/700, Screen title 28pt/700, Row header 22pt/700, Section header 20pt/700
- Episode title 16pt/600, Tile title 15pt/600, Body 15pt/400, Metadata 13pt/400
- Tile subtitle 12pt/400, Uppercase label 11pt/700, Primary button 16pt/700, Secondary button 15pt/600, Tab label 10pt/600, Badge 11pt/700

COMPONENTS:
- Primary Play CTA: 52pt tall, 8pt radius, #00A8E1 fill, dark-navy (#0F171E) label — NOT white, soft blue glow shadow rgba(0,168,225,0.32) 0 8px 24px, pressed → #008CBD + scale 0.97
- Watchlist toggle: a plus icon that becomes a blue checkmark on add, with a success haptic
- Content tile: 2:3 (130pt) or 16:9 (200pt) width, 6pt radius, optional Included with Prime ribbon or blue progress bar for continue-watching
- X-Ray overlay (the signature feature): slides up from the bottom over the lower ~40% of playing video, rgba(35,47,62,0.96) with 24px blur, horizontal strip of circular cast headshots, a now playing track row, dismissed via a downward chevron — never a full-screen modal
- Hero billboard: ~440pt full-bleed auto-still, bottom-up gradient, metadata line with an IMDb-yellow rating segment
- Bottom tab bar: 52pt + safe area, active tab = blue icon AND label (blue is the indicator itself)

LAYOUT:
- 4pt base spacing unit, scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/52/64
- 16pt horizontal margins; rows snap-paginate with a gentle stop, last tile peeks at the edge
- Radius scale: 0 (billboard/backdrop/video), 6pt (content tiles/posters), 8pt (buttons/cards/search), 12-16pt (sheets/X-Ray panel top corners), 500pt (filter chips/badges), 50% (avatars/headshots)

MOTION:
- Tile press scale 1.0→1.04 over 180ms ease-out with a focus shadow + blue ring; Play CTA tap scale-0.97 spring (damping 0.7); X-Ray slide-up 280ms ease-out; watchlist add morphs plus-to-check with a scale bounce 250ms + success haptic; rows snap-decelerate to a tile boundary
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. When a bright, saturated accent color is used as a large button fill, test whether dark text or white text reads better against it before defaulting to white — a sufficiently light/bright accent (like a cyan-blue) can actually contrast better with a dark label, which also lets the accent stay unmistakably vivid.
2. If the catalog mixes included content with paid add-on storefronts in the same rows, always label which is which directly on the tile (a ribbon or badge) — conflating the two erodes trust the first time a user hits a paywall they didn't expect.
3. Any contextual info overlay triggered during video playback should cover only a portion of the frame and never pause the content — the point of a contextual layer is to add information without asking the user to choose between watching and learning more.
4. Restrict a type system to three weights maximum (e.g. regular/semibold/bold) for a functional, non-decorative video app — extra weights add inconsistency risk without adding real hierarchy value at these type sizes.
5. Use horizontal row snap-pagination (not free scroll) when rows are meant to feel like a browsable, discrete set of options rather than an infinite feed — snap communicates these are the choices more clearly than a scroll that trails off.
6. Give any save for later action (watchlist, favorite, follow) a state-morph animation plus a success haptic on add — a static icon swap under-communicates that the action actually took effect.
7. Keep the video player's true-black background completely separate from the app's ambient dark canvas color — using the exact same value for both means a video that hasn't loaded yet is visually indistinguishable from the surrounding chrome.
8. Lock browse/library screens to portrait and let only the player itself rotate to landscape — supporting rotation everywhere adds real engineering cost for a browsing experience that rarely benefits from landscape.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / working title: ___
- Does the catalog mix free/included content with paid add-on channels or subscriptions?: ___
- Primary accent color (hex, or describe the brand color): ___
- Should CTA text be light or dark on that accent — or should I recommend one?: ___
- Does the app need a contextual in-playback overlay (cast info, extra facts, live stats)?: ___
- Existing typography choice, if any: ___
- Target iOS minimum version: ___
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>

2. A content-tile spec distinguishing included/free content from paid-storefront content if the project needs that distinction.
3. If relevant, a contextual playback-overlay component spec modeled on the reference's partial-coverage, non-pausing approach.
4. A hero billboard spec and a bottom tab bar spec matching the reference's active-state-color-is-the-indicator pattern.
5. A motion table (tile press, CTA tap, overlay slide-up/down, save-to-list morph) with durations and easing.
6. A responsive table across at least 4 breakpoints, plus orientation rules for browse vs. player.
7. Accessibility notes: contrast validation for the CTA text/fill pairing chosen, and VoiceOver grouping guidance for tiles and the contextual overlay.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>You are a senior iOS design engineer with deep experience building free, ad-supported streaming apps — where catalog breadth and cost-transparency (this is free) are core selling points that the UI needs to actively communicate rather than downplay.</role>

<reference_data>
Source inspiration: a free, ad-supported streaming app on a cool indigo-violet canvas built specifically to make a five-stop purple-to-magenta brand gradient glow, with dense poster rows and an unhidden yellow free tag as a stated feature rather than an apology.

COLOR (dark-only):
- Canvas #0A0A2A, Surface 1 #15153D, Surface 2 #1E1E52, Surface 3 #262666, Divider #2A2A5C
- Brand gradient: Purple #7408FF → Magenta #FF00FF (135deg), with a mid Violet #A12BFF and a Pink #FF4FD8 for text links
- Primary CTA: pure white #FFFFFF fill with indigo-black #0A0A2A text — the single highest-contrast element in the app, never tinted
- FREE tag: yellow #FFD400 fill, #1A0A2A text — the signature promise, always visible, never shrunk
- Text: Primary #FFFFFF, Secondary #B9B9D6 (cool lavender-grey, not neutral gray), Tertiary #7A7AA0
- Semantic: Success #1FD17B, Error #FF4A6E, Live #FF3B5C, Rating amber #FFB020

TYPOGRAPHY (Inter at heavy weights, matching a tight geometric-grotesque brand face):
- Hero title 32pt/900 tracking -0.6pt, Detail title 28pt/800, Row header 22pt/800, Section title 18pt/700
- Body 16pt/400, Card title 15pt/600, Button label 15pt/800, Meta 13pt/500, Caption 12pt/500
- Badge/tag 11pt/700 uppercase +0.4pt tracking, Tab label 10pt/600

COMPONENTS:
- Primary button: white fill, 8pt radius, indigo-black label, 14pt/30pt padding, 48pt tall, pressed → #E6E6F2 + scale 0.98
- Secondary/gradient button: brand gradient fill, used for register/upgrade CTAs only
- Poster card: 2:3 (~100x150pt), 10pt radius, shadow 0 6px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.45), FREE tag top-left, optional gradient progress bar on the bottom edge for continue-watching, focused state gets a 2pt gradient ring + scale 1.04
- Featured hero: ~230pt tall, inset 14pt from screen edges with an 18pt radius (full-bleed on detail pages), gradient-brand TUBI ORIGINAL pill top-left
- Live TV EPG row: channel logo tile + horizontally-scrolling program blocks; the On-Now block gets a 3pt gradient left border and a faint gradient wash
- Bottom tab bar: 56pt + safe area, magenta active icon/label, no pill indicator

LAYOUT:
- 4pt base spacing unit, scale 4/8/12/14/16/20/24/32/40/48/64
- 16pt screen inset, 10pt poster gutter, rows deliberately bleed off the right edge to signal more to scroll
- Radius scale: 0 (full-bleed hero/backdrop), 4pt (progress/tiny tags), 8pt (buttons/search), 10pt (posters/channel tiles/program blocks/pills), 18pt (inset hero), 20pt (sheets), 500pt (badges), 50% (avatars)

MOTION:
- Hero cross-dissolve every ~6s over 400ms, with a slow ken-burns drift on the backdrop; poster focus/press scale 1.0→1.04 over 150ms ease-out with a gradient-ring fade-in; wordmark shimmer once per launch over 800ms; add-to-list morphs plus-to-check with a 250ms spring + success flash + soft haptic
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. If the product's core value proposition is this costs nothing, put a visible, undiminished tag communicating that on every relevant piece of content — treating a cost-transparency signal as something to hide contradicts the product's own pitch.
2. Pack content rows densely (more visible items, tighter gutters) rather than airily when the pitch is catalog breadth — generous whitespace signals curation and scarcity, which works against a thousands of titles message.
3. Keep the single highest-priority action (the main watch/play button) in a completely neutral color (pure white or black) even when the brand itself is a colorful gradient — the CTA's job is to out-contrast every gradient-colored badge and card around it, and a brand-tinted CTA competes with its own supporting cast.
4. When a brand identity is a multi-stop gradient rather than a single hue, fix its angle and stop order as a reusable asset rather than letting each screen improvise a new gradient — inconsistent gradient direction reads as different brands on different screens.
5. Let poster rows bleed past the right edge of the screen rather than stopping flush with the margin — a visible partial card at the edge is a stronger there's more signal than a hard stop.
6. Reserve heavy display weights (800–900) exclusively for titles and headers, never for body or metadata — the entire weight-contrast hierarchy collapses if secondary text creeps up to a heavy weight too.
7. Use a cool secondary-text tone (lavender-gray, slate) rather than neutral warm gray when the canvas itself has a cool cast — warm gray on a cool-tinted dark background reads as a mismatch even at low opacity.
8. Give focused/selected cards a combined color-plus-scale treatment (a colored ring AND a size bump) rather than either alone — color alone fails for accessibility, scale alone is easy to miss at a glance.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / working title: ___
- Is the core pitch free/ad-supported, subscription, or a mix?: ___
- Brand identity: single accent color or a multi-stop gradient? (describe or paste swatches): ___
- Does the catalog need a Live-TV/EPG component alongside on-demand rows?: ___
- How should free (or any core cost/value message) be visually communicated on content cards?: ___
- Existing typography choice, if any: ___
- Target iOS minimum version: ___
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI Color + gradient + Font token file mapped onto the user's brand, preserving the neutral-CTA-vs-colorful-brand split and the cost/value-tag convention.
2. A dense poster-row and poster-card spec, including the focus/selection treatment and any progress-bar variant for in-progress content.
3. A featured-hero spec and, if needed, a Live-TV EPG row spec adapted to the project's brand.
4. A bottom tab bar spec matching the reference's single-color active-state pattern.
5. A motion table (hero cross-dissolve, card focus, list-add morph) with durations and easing.
6. A responsive table across at least 4 breakpoints showing how card density and hero height change.
7. Accessibility notes: contrast on the CTA and cost/value tag, and how any gradient-only visual signal gets a redundant non-color cue.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>You are a senior iOS design engineer specializing in live-streaming and real-time community apps, with a strong point of view on keeping a this is happening now signal completely separate from a take this action signal, and on designing chat surfaces dense enough to keep up with real-time community throughput.</role>

<reference_data>
Source inspiration: a live-streaming and community app on a near-black canvas whose entire color language is built on a strict two-way split — one hue means act (follow, subscribe, navigate), a completely different hue means this is live right now — plus a chat surface designed for high message density.

COLOR:
- Canvas #0E0E10 (near-black with a faint cool tint; pure #000000 reserved for full-screen/theater video only), Surface 1 #18181B, Surface 2 #1F1F23, Surface 3/Divider #2A2A2D
- Text: Primary #EFEFF1 (intentionally off-white, not pure white — softer for long reading sessions), Secondary #ADADB8, Tertiary #6F6F7B
- Brand/action: Purple #9146FF (pressed #772CE8), used for Follow/Subscribe, active tab, links, focus rings, and the avatar ring in its non-live state
- Liveness (reserved, never used for anything else): Red #EB0400 (pressed #C20300)
- Semantic: Online presence green #00C16E, at-mention highlight rgba(145,70,255,0.20), Error red (shares the live-red hue)

TYPOGRAPHY (Roobert, Inter as free fallback — weights limited to 400/600/700):
- Screen title 28pt/700, Channel-name hero 22pt/700, Section header 20pt/700, Stream title 16pt/600
- Channel label 15pt/700, Body 15pt/400, Chat message 14pt/400, Chat username 14pt/700
- Metadata 13pt/400, Card subtitle 12pt/400, Uppercase label 11pt/700, Primary button 15pt/700, Tab label 10pt/600, Badge 11pt/700

COMPONENTS:
- Primary CTA (Follow/Subscribe): 40pt tall, 6pt radius, purple fill, white label, purple glow shadow rgba(145,70,255,0.35) 0 6px 18px, pressed → #772CE8 + scale 0.97
- Live thumbnail card: 16:9, 6pt radius, a red LIVE pill top-left AND a black viewer-count pill bottom-left (both always present together, never just one)
- Channel avatar live-ring: 2pt ring around the circular avatar — purple in the normal/brand state, switching to red specifically when that channel is currently live
- Chat message row: 4pt vertical / 12pt horizontal padding (deliberately tight for throughput), colored bold username + regular-weight message body, inline 24-28pt emote chips baseline-aligned with text
- Theater-mode chat overlay: on rotation to landscape/theater, the docked chat column becomes a semi-transparent rgba(14,14,16,0.72) blurred panel floating over the right third of full-screen video — never hidden, never a full modal
- Bottom tab bar: 52pt + safe area, purple active icon/label (purple is the indicator, not a pill)

LAYOUT:
- 4pt base spacing unit, scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/52/64
- 16pt horizontal margins on non-chat surfaces; chat lines use a tight 4pt vertical rhythm specifically to maximize message throughput per screen
- Radius scale: 0 (theater/full-bleed video), 4pt (LIVE pill/viewer pill/sub badges), 6pt (thumbnails/primary CTA/cards), 8pt (search/chat input/chips), 12-16pt (sheets/emote picker), 500pt (filter chips), 50% (avatars)

MOTION:
- LIVE pill: continuous 1.6s pulse (scale + opacity 1.0→0.5→1.0) — the only continuously-looping animation in the system besides chat scroll; card press scale 1.0→1.03 over 180ms; chat messages slide up 8pt + fade in over 120ms on arrival; viewer count rolls (odometer-style) on update; theater toggle expands video over 250ms while chat cross-fades from docked to overlay
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Assign exactly one color to take an action (follow, subscribe, primary navigation) and a completely different, unrelated color to this is happening live right now, and never let the two swap roles anywhere in the product — a user should be able to glance at a screen and know instantly which color means what, every time.
2. Use an intentionally off-white (not pure #FFFFFF) for primary text on a near-black canvas when the product involves extended reading (chat, comments, long feeds) — pure white at high contrast becomes fatiguing over a long session; a slightly dimmed off-white reduces that without looking washed out.
3. Pair a live-status pill with a viewer-count or activity pill rather than showing either alone — liveness plus scale (how many people) together communicate this matters right now more completely than either fact by itself.
4. Encode a live/active state directly on an identity element (like an avatar ring) in addition to any badge — a ring around a profile picture is legible even when scanning a dense list quickly, before any text is read.
5. Keep chat or any real-time message list at a tight vertical rhythm (as little padding as legibility allows) — the entire value of a live chat surface is throughput; generous spacing directly reduces how much conversation is visible at once.
6. When a docked side panel (like chat) needs to coexist with full-screen content, make it a translucent, blurred overlay rather than either hiding it completely or keeping it as an opaque panel that steals screen space — the goal is co-presence of content and community, not a forced choice between them.
7. Reserve continuous/looping animation (a pulse, a marquee) for exactly one this is live signal — if multiple elements pulse or loop simultaneously, the eye stops knowing where to look and the technique loses its power.
8. Treat inline emotes/reaction images as first-class typographic elements (baseline-aligned, sized relative to surrounding text) rather than oversized stickers — chat needs to read as one continuous line of communication, not text interrupted by graphics.
</house_rules>

<the_project>

- Does this app have a real-time chat, comment stream, or activity feed component?: ___
- Brand/action color and a separate, unrelated live/active now signal color: ___
- Does the app need a theater/full-screen mode where a side panel needs to coexist with video or main content?: ___
- Does the community support custom emotes, reactions, or inline media tokens in messages?: ___
- Existing typography choice, if any: ___
- Target iOS minimum version: ___
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI Color + Font token file mapped onto the user's brand, enforcing the strict two-role color split between action/brand and liveness/activity signals.
2. A live/activity thumbnail or feed-item card spec including the paired status-plus-count-pill pattern.
3. A dense chat or activity-feed row spec, including any inline emote/reaction token treatment.
4. A theater/full-screen-mode overlay spec (if relevant) describing how a side panel becomes translucent over full-bleed content.
5. A motion table covering the continuous live pulse, message/item arrival animation, and any counter-rolling animation.
6. A responsive table across at least 4 breakpoints plus orientation rules for browse vs. theater/full-screen mode.
7. Accessibility notes: how the live/active state is conveyed to VoiceOver and color-blind users beyond the color split alone, and how a live message region should be exposed for screen readers.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>You are a senior iOS design engineer who specializes in high-volume, content-forward video-feed apps — the kind where a single card layout gets repeated thousands of times per session, so every pixel of that one component matters far more than any hero screen.</role>

<reference_data>
Source inspiration: a massive-scale video platform whose entire visual identity rests on one repeated card (a hard-edged thumbnail + metadata), a single reserved brand red used almost nowhere except one button and a few static marks, and a persistent floating mini-player as a signature navigation pattern.

COLOR (supports both light and dark, same brand red in both):
- Light: Canvas #FFFFFF, Surface 1 #F9F9F9, Surface 2 #F2F2F2, Divider #E5E5E5, Text Primary #0F0F0F, Secondary #606060, Tertiary #909090
- Dark: Canvas #0F0F0F (a deliberately not-quite-black brand token, never pure #000000), Surface 1 #1F1F1F, Surface 2 #272727, Surface 3 #3F3F3F, Divider #303030, Text Primary #FFFFFF, Secondary #AAAAAA, Tertiary #717171
- Brand: YouTube Red #FF0000 (pressed #CC0000) — reserved for the Subscribe button (unsubscribed state), the LIVE pill, the logomark, and unread-notification dots ONLY
- Info blue #3EA6FF for inline links only; Warning yellow #FFC400 rarely, for age-restriction notices

TYPOGRAPHY (YouTube Sans for display moments, Roboto for everything else, weights 400/500/700 only):
- Screen title 20pt/700 (YouTube Sans), Video-detail title 18pt/600, Video title (feed) 16pt/500 — the single most common type moment in the app, 2-line clamp
- Channel name 14pt/500, Metadata 13pt/400 (1.2M views · 3 days ago), Comment text 14pt/400, Comment author 13pt/500
- Button (Subscribe) 14pt/500, Chip 14pt/400, Tab label 10pt/500, Duration tag 11pt/500

COMPONENTS:
- Subscribe button: 36pt tall, 18pt corner radius (a rounded rectangle, deliberately NOT a full pill), red #FF0000 fill with white text when unsubscribed; morphs to a gray #F2F2F2/#272727 fill with primary-color text plus a trailing bell icon once subscribed; 200ms spring morph with a haptic
- Video card (the atomic unit): full-width 16:9 thumbnail with ZERO corner radius (hard edges are the load-bearing aesthetic), a bottom-right duration tag on rgba(0,0,0,0.75) with white text, a top-left red LIVE pill when applicable, then a metadata row (28pt avatar + 2-line title + one-line channel/metadata string)
- Filter chip row: default gray pill, but the SELECTED chip fully inverts (black background/white text in light mode, or the reverse in dark) rather than just tinting
- Mini-player: 72pt tall, docked above the tab bar, persists while the user browses elsewhere — described as the single most distinctive navigation pattern in the app; drag up expands via shared-element animation, drag down past a threshold dismisses

<house_rules>
1. When one component (a card, a row) will be rendered hundreds or thousands of times per session, spend disproportionate design effort on that single component — a 2px error in a hero screen is invisible next to a 2px error repeated across an entire feed.
2. Reserve a brand color for a short, explicit, named list of elements (one button, one status pill, the logo) and never let it become a general-purpose accent — the moment the color shows up on more than a handful of things, it stops reading as the brand and starts reading as decoration.
3. If a subscribe/follow/save action has an active and inactive visual state, make the active state visually calmer (grayer, quieter) than the inactive one — the CTA should be loud when it's asking for the action, and quiet once it's confirmed, so attention naturally moves to the next unconverted item.
4. Decide deliberately whether card art gets rounded corners or hard edges, and apply that choice with zero exceptions across the entire feed — a single rounded thumbnail in an otherwise hard-edged feed reads as a bug, not a variant.
5. If content can persist across navigation (audio, video, a background task), give it a persistent, draggable, dismissible mini-surface rather than pausing or hiding it when the user navigates away — forcing a stop-to-navigate tradeoff measurably hurts engagement in any app where content has real duration.
6. When a filter or toggle chip is selected, prefer full color inversion over a lighter tint — inversion is unambiguous at a glance, a tint can be missed at low contrast or on partially-visible chips at the edge of a scroll.
7. Support both light and dark canvases with the same brand accent color unchanged, but let neutral canvas/surface/text tokens fully re-map — the accent is the brand identity across appearance modes; everything else should adapt to reduce eye strain in each mode.
8. Keep any interaction count that could be used to shame or harass a user (like a public negative-reaction count) hidden from other viewers by default — a stated product decision that measurably reduced negative pile-on behavior in the reference app, worth considering for any UGC-adjacent metric.
</house_rules>
